bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: I would not; a recruiter sets up a role when we open a vacancy and I only hear about it in passing.
bundles.why: It is the recruiters' setup chore, and I only care that the blocking of protected traits keeps us out of legal trouble.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Only if a recruiter mentions in the weekly catch-up that uploading CVs is quicker now.
bundles.why: It is plumbing I never see, though I would assume any tool reads CVs somehow.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: When the CEO asks who the best three for the data role are and I want a shortlist to point at.
bundles.why: I want a shortlist for the CEO; a filtered list that is not ranked is not what I expected, but a person signing off is defensible under HR law.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: When a recruiter tells me a candidate is interview-ready and checked, before I hear it from the hiring manager.
bundles.why: Checked claims reduce the risk of a bad hire and an embarrassing mistake, but I only care about the result, not the process.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: When a rejected candidate complains or threatens a claim and I need to show what we told them.
bundles.why: Specific, approved feedback protects the company legally and from bad reviews, but it is not what I open the tool for.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: My weekly five-minute check on a laptop, before the CEO meeting, to get a number showing hiring got faster.
bundles.why: It is the only screen I personally use and the only one that gives me an answer for the CEO; without it I stop using the tool.

proof_timing.why: Asking for documents up front puts people off applying and looks heavy-handed, while asking only the shortlisted, with a reason, is fair and easy to defend.
